slides.text: AI Updates Grok 4.5 by xAI/SpaceXAI (July 8-9) coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work 1.5 Trillion-parameter V9 foundation Trained with Cursor coding data It targets Opus-class performance The model is optimized for tools and agents, aiming to power autonomous workflows for soft.dev. & research Grok 4.5 is being positioned as a cheaper, high-capability alternative to leading models Pricing $2 / $6 in/out per 1M (compare $5 / $25 Claude Opus) OpenAI GPT‑5.6 models: Sol, Terra, Luna (July 9) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mD1F5DsC5tc Pricing -  in/out per 1M token Sol - $5 / $30, the flagship Terra - $2.50/$15 - balanced, like 5.5 Luna $1/$6 - fastest and most affordable 1.5M-token context window Gemini 3.5 Flash (May 19) $1.5 / $9 Gemini 3.5 Pro (still in limited preview) $2.5 / $15 Anthropic’s Fable 5 promo for subscriptions Through July 12 Fable 5 is available as part of your subscription (up to 50% of your weekly limits) Starting July 13 Fable 5 will no longer be part of subscriptions. It will require "usage credits" Re-release of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models Anthropic introduced a strict, government collaborated safety classifier However, this classifier frequently flags harmless coding or biology prompts, automatically downgrading paying users to the older, cheaper Opus 4.8 model. slides.title: AI Updates Instruct Claude to Modify its own
slides.text: AI Updates Instruct Claude to Modify its own Claude.md file Paste this into claude to build 10x faster... (Boris Cherny Method) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9nTG1B1No_E At the end of your claude.md file add this phrase under a dedicated section (like # Self-Learning or # Instructions): When I correct you or catch you making a mistake before continuing add the lesson as a oneline rule under #lessons so it never happens again This instructs Claude to update its own markdown file. When a user corrects Claude, the AI automatically appends that mistake as a one-line rule under a dedicated lessons section. Boris Cherny of Anthropic on 5 new roles Instead of traditional roles like engineer or designer hire for five archetypes: Prototypers: generate many ideas Builders: turn the best ones into real products Sweepers: refine systems, remove bad ideas, and improve quality Growers: focus on product-market fit using data and user feedback Maintainers: ensure systems stay reliable and scalable over time The mix depends on stage: early teams need prototypers, builders, and sweepers; growth adds growers; mature products rely more on sweepers, growers, and maintainers Hire based on function and impact, not job titles or resumes https://x.com/bcherny/status/2071379474277613732 What is missing? Boris Cherny has described only roles for implementation of the idea. But who formulates this idea? We need to have someone like Steve Jobs - a visionary. Someone to define a direction, goal, intent, strategy We need someone who knows where to hit. Remember this old story: A factory machine breaks down. A consultant taps one spot with a hammer and the machine starts. His invoices $1 for hitting, and $9,999 for knowing where to hit. Dan Sullivan from Strategic Coach explains how business owners do everything themselves behave as "self-milking cow" - He encourages business leaders to delegate, build systems, and find the "Who" to execute tasks

slides.title: AI Updates OpenAI optimizations cut inference cost x2
slides.text: AI Updates OpenAI optimizations cut inference cost x2 Serve ChatGPT for logged‑out users with only a few hundred NVIDIA GPUs, versus far larger fleets before They have not disclosed details, but observers believe it’s a combination of aggressive quantization, smarter KV caching, highly efficient batching, and routing simpler queries to cheaper models, all backed by better low‑level kernel and serving‑stack tuning The business impact is significant: cheaper inference can support lower API prices, higher usage limits, and better profit margins So inference efficiency is a key competitive moat DeepSeek DSpark Speculative Decoding Accelerates AI generation speed by 80+% Increases total output capacity by 700% without losing quality Traditional speculative decoding uses small models to draft text ahead for a larger model to verify, but drafts are often slow or error-prone due to sentence decay DSpark fixes this by using a parallel drafter enhanced with a lightweight Markov head to eliminate errors It also introduces a confidence head that dynamically adjusts draft lengths based on context predictability - like shortening drafts for creative tasks and lengthening them for deterministic coding Finally, DSpark is hardware-aware, regulating drafts based on real-time GPU loads to optimize multi-user data centers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J0D7qV3nl7w Z.ai GLM-5.2 + DeepSeek's DSpark Beats Claude + 85% Faster + OpenSource + Affordable https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wDpN2ORnqZk

slides.text: AI Updates Organization-wide Agent - Andrej Karpathy https://x.com/karpathy/status/2069547676849557725 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eMVaGOsfYs8 from (1) isolated web chatbots and (2) desktop apps to (3) persistent, organization-wide AI entities Anthropic’s Tag feature in Slack - generates 65% of Anthropic's internal product code ! AI can now act as an active, multiplayer "employee" deeply integrated across a company’s entire system, tools, and context. "Claude Tag" is currently only for Team/Enterprise A small businesses can build a similar functionality using custom Telegram bots connected via AWS and tools like Composio Composio SKD connects agents to 100s of apps (GitHub, Slack, Salesforce, Notion, Jira, Gmail, databases, OS tools) It handles authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT(JSON Web Token)), sandboxed execution, logging, and dashboards so you don’t have to hand‑roll API glue and infra for each tool This makes it useful for turning agent prototypes into production workflows like code assistants, sales bots, or admin helpers https://composio.dev https://github.com/ComposioHQ/composio https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-skjxykuajjn34 https://github.com/ComposioHQ/composio/blob/master/docs/introduction/intro/overview.mdx

slides.title: Sentdex Sentdex - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AgpeggCsRH4 Running AI Locally Doesn't
slides.text: Sentdex Sentdex - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AgpeggCsRH4 Running AI Locally Doesn't Require an Expensive Setup A single consumer GPU like an RTX 3090 or 4090 can handle roughly 70% to 90% of local coding and general Q&A model needs GLM-52 Quantizations - standard 8-bit KV caching significantly degrades GLM-52's performance after 1k to 8k context lengths. Switching to a 16-bit KV cache fixes this Using Terminal Bench v2.1 for long-horizon agentic coding tests, he found that a highly compressed 2-bit quantization of GLM-52 performs almost identically to the 4-bit version Scaling "test-time compute" (allowing a model more tokens to actively reason through a problem before answering) significantly levels the playing field. Even a fundamentally "dumber" model can achieve incredible benchmark results if it is allowed to reason for a long time. Because of this, he argues that closed-source giants have no permanent moat over open-source alternatives DeepSeek V4 Flash - very fast and extremely cheap via providers like Open Router (roughly 14 cents per million input tokens) Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B / Qwen 2.5 Coder - work on single 24GB GPU (especially good when paired with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) to maximize tokens-per-second) Agents Hermes (general purpose) & Minion (for coding) Sentdex - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=31MvP7yHzxM Running AI Locally for software engineering Half of coding tasks can be done with local models like Qwen 32B or 27B, relying on cloud APIs only when needed DeepSeek V4 Flash is best for fully local setup. MoE, 13B active, runs fast at native precision via vLLM and tensor parallelism Aggressive quantization, like dropping to an 8-bit KV cache, severely tanks model intelligence Ultimately, fast local models excel when developers remain in the loop to guide them.

slides.text: AI Updates Open Knowledge Format (OKF) from Google Open Standard for the Karpathy LLM Wiki https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T33iI6izAKw https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VHKXIHP4i10 OKF is a standardized file format consisting of structured Markdown documents OKF operates like a curated, cross-linked wiki handbook that an AI agent can directly read, navigate, and update Claude in Chrome is Anthropic’s official Chrome extension It lets Claude see the page you have open, understand its structure, and then take actions like clicking buttons, following links, filling forms, and extracting or summarizing information Combined with Claude Code, you can build or modify a web app in the terminal, then have Claude in Chrome open and exercise the running app to test flows and catch issues without manual copy‑paste Functionally, it turns Claude from a pure chat assistant into a lightweight browser automation agent that operates within your existing authenticated Chrome session https://claude.com/claude-for-chrome https://claude.ai/chrome https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-for-chrome https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome

slides.title: AI Updates Use Python to make Karpathy-style wiki
slides.text: AI Updates Use Python to make Karpathy-style wiki https://towardsdatascience.com/llm-wikis-are-over-engineered-i-replaced-mine-with-a-pure-python-compiler/ KV (Key-Value) Cache and PagedAttention These are open-source mechanisms from the vLLM inference engine - used to speed up LLMs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o0gkdZBtwEg During LLM inference, the prefill phase processes the prompt, while the decode phase generates tokens sequentially Normally, generating a new token requires recomputing all previous tokens, which degrades performance KV caching prevents this by saving past key-value matrices However, standard KV caching creates fragmented memory by pre-allocating large, rigid slots PagedAttention solves this by breaking the cache into small, non-contiguous pages mapped dynamically, cutting memory waste by up to 80% The video concludes with optimization tips, including .. tuning memory utilization .. enabling prefix caching .. using chunked prefill How to Talk to Claude https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OgT1Or4OP1k Cal Hyslop explains that you should shift from asking simple questions to providing 3 things: - context - outcome (what is required) - role (to expose blind spots and analyze decisions)

slides.title: AI Updates Three AI world model paradigms: Meta’s
slides.text: AI Updates Three AI world model paradigms: Meta’s JEPA, WorldLabs’ taxonomy, Einstein World Models concept JEPA focuses on learning world within an abstract latent space WorldLabs structures world models into renderers, simulators, and planners Einstein World Models framework from MBZUAI (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE) treats world models as modular tools. LLMs remain the primary reasoner, calling on visual world modules to perform thought experiments when linguistic reasoning falls short The speaker argues that unified embedding architectures like JEPA may fail, predicting that future AI will favor modular, tool-based visual physics simulations controlled by LLMs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tv17bmE2FNY JEPA is just LoRA in disguise JEPA acts as a matrix factorization mechanism creating a low-rank approximation of the world's transition dynamics New research from Peking University and the University of Sydney provides a math explanation of Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) By filtering out high-dimensional visual noise like pixels, JEPA focuses purely on action-relevant movements This dynamic creates a critical balance between approximation error and sample complexity error Drawing a parallel to low-rank adaptation (LoRA) in language models, the host introduces a novel concept: creating "JEPA adapters." These specialized add-ons could efficiently fine-tune foundational world models for specific domains, such as medical robotics, without intensive retraining https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2RVz67hxSAU

slides.title: AI Updates AI has not made people universally
slides.text: AI Updates AI has not made people universally better It amplifies existing skill levels Skilled engineers use it to dramatically increase productivity, turning weeks of work into hours Unskilled users generate fragile code, technical debt, and costly failures they cannot diagnose. Real-world incidents show how misuse leads to security breaches, data loss, and wasted resources The market reflects this divide: top-tier models drive innovation, while cheaper alternatives commoditize routine tasks Meanwhile, a growing ecosystem resells access and exploits leaked API keys Ultimately, AI rewards strong fundamentals and punishes their absence, widening the gap between competent professionals and those relying blindly on automation. https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/learned-helplessness-service-viacheslav-kasatkin-dvupc/ Meta Brain2Qwerty v2 Measures magnetic field around the head using MEG (Magneto-Encephalography scanner) Uses AI to decode brain activity into text while the patient is typing 61% average word accuracy, peaking at 78% for the top participant Requires giant laboratory equipment Holds massive long-term potential for paralyzed patients

slides.title: AI Updates 10 core components of an AI
slides.text: AI Updates 10 core components of an AI agent harness: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mQfTdNVCOB0 Instructions - rules, prompts, styling guides Context Delivery - read files, stack traces, relevant data Context Management - filter and compresses transcripts, re-rank data, reduce noise Tool Interface (schemas, MCP) to request actions Execution Environment (sandbox, container) Durable State - persistence mechanism (database, memory) Orchestration - retry, step-by-step, human approval gates Sub-Agents - delegating specialized sub-tasks Skills and Procedures - reusable playbooks and checklists Verification & Observability - test output, logs for debugging Claude Design’s June 2026 update Adds proper design system imports, a better canvas editor, and tighter Claude Code integration You can now use real components from your GitHub or design files, edit layouts directly on a canvas, and sync designs with code in both directions The goal is to keep work on-brand while reducing token usage in everyday product design workflows https://claude2video.com/blog/claude-design-june-2026-update

slides.text: AI Updates Alex Hormozi's three-folder organization for AI Agent " Business Context " - md files - company's identity, target audience, brand voice, and goals " Data " - raw training materials, such as past newsletters, to help the AI mirror specific tones and writing cadences " Prompts " - highly detailed, reusable prompt templates specifying strict roles, rules, and structures https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q1_AjJAmDGY

slides.title: llama.cpp llama.cpp "finetune" utility was removed Current versions
slides.text: llama.cpp llama.cpp "finetune" utility was removed Current versions focus on inference, quantization, and serving You can fine-tune your model today using a PyTorch-based stack (e.g., TRL or LLaMA-Factory) and then convert the resulting Hugging Face model to GGUF for high-performance CPU or edge inference with llama.cpp This lets you leverage robust training tooling while still using llama.cpp where it excels: lightweight, fast local serving of already fine-tuned models https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/213701b51a17175d0d326b566efc03f30ec7fbe6/examples/finetune Accelerating llama.cpp using Claude Fable 5 Codacus uses Claude 5 Fable to optimize the llama.cpp codebase on a mid-range local AI rig The AI analyzed the software, profiled performance, and achieved a massive 64.5% speedup in prefill prompt processing. Claude discovered that the GPU sits idle over 41% of the time waiting for MoE model weights to transfer from system RAM across the slow PCIe bus To fix this, the AI enabled pinned mmapped memory for faster transfers and restructured the pipeline to upload expert layers in parallel while the GPU computes attention. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VytSYCDhWQ0 llama.cpp https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp Georgi Gerganov

slides.text: AI Updates Open Source Repos for Claude Code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IRPEfl2BD_c Claude Video - https://github.com/bradautomates/claude-video - video ingestion - transcribes audio via Groq's free Whisper model and intelligently extracts keyframes NotebookLM-MCP - https://github.com/topics/google-notebooklm - brings Google’s NotebookLM into the Claude Code terminal, allows you to offload huge document research and synthesis tasks to Google's servers for free Graphify - https://graphify.net - maps codebases by compressing files into a knowledge graph of nodes and clusters (not needing expensive vector DBs) Obsidian Skills - https://github.com/topics/google-notebooklm - compact repo trains Claude Code on best practices for managing markdown files, PDFs, and media assets within an Obsidian notebook Impeccable - https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable - open-source design tool Ponytail - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xuFcmUAQUc - A token-efficiency plugin outputting up to 54% fewer lines of code Evolution of RAG - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyQ4ffFU27Y Naive RAG - simple semantic vector searches - suffers from strict chunking limitations. Advanced RAG  - adding pre-retrieval (multi-query expansion) and post-retrieval reranking algorithms GraphRAG - structured knowledge graphs map relationships across documents Agentic RAG - handles queries using autonomous reasoning loops to dynamically choose tools, trading high latency for maximum flexibility
